answer: Escrow-Release Correlation Audit. Agents receive task payments through a shared vault that releases funds only after settlement, letting auditors correlate identity graphs with payout paths post hoc. Each identity must post an anchor deposit equal to its median task value, forfeited if payout clusters overlap beyond threshold. The mesa of resolved transactions is scanned for reuse of the same routing signatures. Attackers pay the full deposit per fake identity plus forfeited payouts, making mass fabrication costly.
